script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: ambition

Begin screenplay.

---

Title: The Unstoppable Cinnamon Roll

INT. KITCHEN - MORNING

JAMES, 35, a charismatic man with glasses and a mustache, stands over a kitchen counter, his face buried in a cookbook. He sighs and wipes his brow.

JAMES
(to himself)
How am I supposed to become a master chef without a proper kitchen?

His wife, LUCY, 33, a vibrant woman with auburn hair, enters from the living room, carrying a tray of coffees.

LUCY
(smiling)
Well, you could start by making breakfast for our family instead of ordering takeout every night.

JAMES
(disappointed)
That's not the same thing, Lucy. I want to make a difference in the world, and becoming a master chef is my dream.

Lucy sets the tray down on the counter and sits next to her husband.

LUCY
I understand your ambition, James, but we have bills to pay, and a family to feed. We can't just quit our jobs and open a restaurant.

JAMES
(frustrated)
But that's exactly what we need to do! I can't let my dreams slip away.

INT. JAMES' OFFICE - DAY

James sits at his desk, staring at a computer screen filled with job listings. A coworker, MARK, 42, enters, looking exhausted.

MARK
(sighing)
Another long night, huh?

JAMES
(disengaged)
Yeah, the same old thing. I can't take it anymore, Mark. I need to do something with my life.

MARK
(surprised)
Really? What are you thinking about?

JAMES
(determined)
I'm going to become a master chef.

Mark raises an eyebrow.

MARK
And how do you plan on doing that, with no experience or money?

JAMES
(smiling)
I'll figure it out. I always do.

INT. COMMUNITY CENTER - NIGHT

James attends a cooking class taught by CHEF LEE, 55, a stern yet compassionate woman. He eagerly absorbs every word she says, taking copious notes.

CHEF LEE
(to the class)
Cooking is an art form, and like any other art, it takes practice and dedication.

JAMES
(excitedly)
I'm ready to dedicate my life to it!

INT. JAMES' KITCHEN - DAY

James practices his newfound skills, making pancakes for his family. They sit at the table, marveling at his improvement.

LUCY
(tearfully)
I'm so proud of you, James. Keep going.

James smiles, feeling a renewed sense of purpose.

INT. APPLICATION ROOM - DAY

James sits in front of a computer, filling out applications to culinary schools. He hits send on the final application, feeling a weight lift off his shoulders.

JAMES
(to himself)
I'm on my way, Lucy. I'm going to become a master chef.

INT. KITCHEN - NIGHT

The family gathers around the table for dinner, James having prepared a gourmet meal. They laugh and enjoy each other's company, feeling a sense of contentment and pride.

LUCY
(smiling at her husband)
I'm so glad you followed your dream, James.

James looks at her, his heart full.

JAMES
Me too, Lucy. Me too.

FADE OUT.

End screenplay.
